tob-4058: In the first volume of Isis Unveiled, Blavatsky takes on the science of her day, holding that book-learned physics missed the living forces behind nature. tob-4158: William James’s Gifford Lectures gather faith’s raw stuff — turnings, answered prayers, saints’ raptures — and weigh what they prove about the mind. tob-4161-70458: Edward Tylor’s Primitive Culture founded man-lore as a science — holding that human belief grows by findable laws, upward from ghost-faith. This first volume treats faith’s springs: spirits, souls, and worship of the dead. The book’s ‘animism’ teaching shaped a hundred years of thought.
tob-0158: Kenneth Guthrie’s rendering gives the Gathas — Zoroaster’s own seventeen hymns, the Avesta’s oldest part. These verses, sung about 1200 B.C., preach the One Wise Lord and the world-battle of good and ill. The Gathas are Zoroastrianism’s headwater.
cia-0000102958: A November 1986 intelligence report on imprisonment inside a prison and work camp in Tashkent, capital of Soviet Uzbekistan. cia-0000108158: An estimate of Finland's situation and likely developments during 1954 — though the archive dates the document itself to January 1964, a puzzle for catalogers. cia-0000109058: A November 1967 report on the Che Guevara diary — the journal of the revolutionary's doomed Bolivian campaign, captured after his execution that October. cia-0000119758: A chronology of the Hungarian Revolution's principal events from October 23 to November 4, 1956 — the whole uprising in sequence. brought-home-pg7358: Hesba Stretton, beloved author of Jessica's First Prayer, tells of a child brought home — a tale of rescue and love. Her tender stories moved Victorian England. Simple, touching, and true-hearted. Waifs, kind strangers, and happy endings fill her gentle pages.
arxiv-2605-08858: Explaining a trained model's decisions usually needs access to its training data — which may be private or gone. Piotr Borycki, Magdalena Trędowicz, Jacek Tabor, and colleagues propose ProDG, which builds prototypes for post-hoc explanations without any data at all, using generative techniques instead. arxiv-2605-09358: 6G dreams of smart surfaces that shape radio waves — beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, integrated with transceivers. Mahmoud Raeisi, Ayoub Ammar Boudjelal, Henk Wymeersch, and colleagues process signals in the wave domain for sustainable, inclusive 6G. The 2026 paper is wireless engineering for the next decade.
arxiv-2605-09458: Composition algebras — the reals, complexes, quaternions, octonions — are the only normed division algebras, and their integral shells carry polytope structure. Daniele Corradetti studies these integral shell polytopes and their combinatorics. The 2026 paper is algebra on the geometry of number systems.
arxiv-2605-09658: Global optimization wanders; regional search zooms — especially on a budget. arxiv-2605-09958: Quantum nonlinear properties certified from a single measurement setting — no need for many. Zihao Li, Datong Chen, Dayue Qin, and colleagues demonstrate it. The 2026 paper is quantum information with minimal assumptions. It squeezes quantum nonlinearity from one setting.
plos-pone-0003458: Cancer researchers measured how a missing repair gene changes mutations in this 2008 mouse study. Ku80 is central to non-homologous end joining, the cell's quick fix for broken DNA, and the team counted mutation rates and patterns at a reporter gene across tissues without it. The results show exactly what kind of genetic errors pile up when that repair pathway is gone.
plos-pone-0003558: Tumor researchers found a precision brake for rogue muscle cells in this 2008 paper. In tuberous sclerosis, loss of the TSC2 gene lets smooth-muscle cells proliferate into tumors, and an antibody against EGFR, the epidermal growth factor receptor, halted that growth specifically. The targeted approach offers hope for a disease with few good options.
plos-pone-0003658: In 2008, Evnouchidou, Momburg, and Papakyriakou studied how the immune system trims its flags. ERAP1, an enzyme in the cell's workshop, cuts long protein pieces down to the right size for display, and the team found the piece's inner sequence decides where the cut falls. The inner code, not just the ends, steers the final trim.
plos-pone-0003758: Sun, Jin, and Xiong brought a classic filter to cell biology in this 2008 paper. Their extended Kalman filter estimates the hidden parameters of nonlinear state-space models of biochemical networks. The method helps turn noisy measurements of living chemistry into working mathematical models.
plos-pone-0003858: In 2008, a team knocked out a multi-tasking receptor in mice. Animals missing GPRC6A developed weak bones, feminization traits, and metabolic syndrome all at once. The triple phenotype reveals one receptor quietly governing bone, sex traits, and metabolism together.
plos-pone-0003958: In 2008, Szendroedi, Zwettler, and Schmid found muscles running low on power after acromegaly. Patients previously treated for growth-hormone excess showed reduced ATP synthesis in skeletal muscle. The lingering deficit links past hormone storms to lasting metabolic weakness.
plos-pone-0004058: In 2008, Gray, Williams, and Li tracked a waterborne parasite across China's wetlands. They modeled transmission dynamics of Schistosoma japonicum in lakes and marshlands. Over a million people are infected, with forty million at risk. The detailed transmission map targets control efforts where the parasite thrives.
plos-pone-0004158: In 2008, Rollin, Blechet, and Regina found location predicting lung cancer fate. Where ID2 protein sat inside cells carried predictive value in non-small cell lung cancer. Nuclear versus cytoplasmic ID2 split patient outlooks. The address beats the amount as a marker.
plos-pone-0004258: In 2009, Smith, Male, and Harper found pig MRSA in the Midwest. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strain ST398 turned up in swine and swine workers. plos-pone-0004358: In 2009, Gottig, Garavaglia, and Garofalo found a citrus killer's grappling hook. A filamentous hemagglutinin-like protein of Xanthomonas citri was characterized. The citrus-canker germ's secretion system was mapped. The finding aids crop defense. The work dissects the type V secretion machinery.
plos-pone-0348858: Extension programs must prove their worth to limited-resource audiences. This paper valued education for these audiences using a willingness-to-accept experiment. The valuations give program planners hard numbers on what their teaching is actually worth to the participants it serves.
plos-pone-0357758: Human metapneumovirus still lacks a vaccine — and this paper jumped the queue computationally. It predicted a multi-epitope vaccine candidate through integrated reverse vaccinology and pan-genomic approaches. The in silico design gives vaccine developers a concrete head start instead of starting from zero.
plos-pone-0357958: Fusing features across an image demands attention that adapts to content — ideally without extra parameters. PSAFM is a parameter-free spatial attention fusion module for vision models. The lightweight design boosts accuracy without the usual parameter bloat, making it cheap to drop into existing networks.
plos-pone-0343858: Drug regulation differs sharply between China and the US — and AI assistants must navigate both. Sino-US-DrugQA is a benchmark for evaluating large language models on cross-jurisdictional pharmaceutical regulation. The test reveals which AI systems can handle the regulatory maze and which ones stumble.
plos-pone-0357458: Trainee translators write English differently from native academic writers — in measurable ways. This comparative analysis examined syntactic complexity in English academic texts by Chinese MTI trainee translators versus native writers. The differences reveal the translator’s syntactic fingerprint and where training should focus.
plos-pone-0357658: Degenerating spinal disks need imaging that goes beyond ordinary CT. This paper tested spectral CT electron density measurements for evaluating lumbar intervertebral disk degeneration. The electron-density maps grade disk decay more precisely, giving spine specialists a sharper tool for diagnosis and surgical planning.
plos-pone-0354458: Finding the exact right moment in a long video demands temporal intelligence. This paper added explicit temporal inductive biases — via multi-scale Gaussian priors — for video moment retrieval. The built-in priors sharpen search, helping systems locate ‘the part where’ with far greater accuracy.
plos-pone-0357158: Highway corridors without fixed sensors still need reliable traffic data. This TomTom–HERE benchmark study tested reproducible floating car data monitoring for data-scarce highway corridors. The head-to-head benchmark shows planners which commercial data source to trust when building their own sensors isn’t an option.
plos-pone-0356258: Freeze-dried PCR reagents could revolutionize diagnostics in places without cold chains. This paper developed and validated a 6-dye lyophilized fluorescent multiplex PCR system. The shelf-stable system detects multiple targets at once, simplifying testing where infrastructure is thinnest.
plos-pone-0348158: Men experience weight loss programs differently — and most programs ignore that. This paper explored male perceptions and experiences of weight loss initiatives, drawing out considerations for sustainable lifestyle practices. The findings push program designers toward approaches men will actually stick with.
plos-pone-0356358: After a heart attack, macrophages and iron-driven cell death — ferroptosis — interact in ways that decide how much heart muscle survives. This bioinformatics analysis identified candidate crosstalk genes linking macrophage activity, ferroptosis, and immune infiltration in myocardial infarction. The gene list nominates new therapeutic targets for limiting cardiac damage.
plos-pone-0346758: Urinary incontinence humiliates frail older adults — yet their voices are rarely heard in treatment design. This qualitative study captured the perspectives of frail older adults and their family caregivers on incontinence interventions. Their candid views point to care that preserves dignity, not just dryness.
plos-pone-0356758: Infertility treatment strains every dimension of a woman’s life — including sexual function. This paper used latent profile analysis to map patterns of female sexual function during IVF embryo transfer in China, plus their influencing factors. The profiles give fertility clinics a framework for addressing what patients rarely voice.
plos-pone-0355558: Laboratory notebooks are going digital — and the transition is bumpier than expected. This paper examined digital transformation in laboratory documentation through an eLabFTW case study plus a survey-informed onboarding framework. The findings give labs a practical roadmap for dragging their record-keeping into the digital age.
plos-pone-0356058: Expansive soils heave and crack with moisture changes — unless reinforced. This paper tested the mechanical properties and freeze–thaw durability of expansive soil reinforced with polypropylene and lignin fibers. The fiber-reinforced soil withstood freezing cycles that destroy untreated ground — promising tougher foundations for cold regions.
plos-pone-0336758: The Amazon’s fish diversity is vast — but eDNA surveys see only what their primers and libraries allow. This paper assessed how primer choice and reference libraries impact fish diversity estimates in eDNA surveys. The methodological findings are a cautionary tale for everyone counting Amazonian fish from water samples.
plos-pone-0355958: Tibial tubercle fractures — where the knee’s growth plate tears — threaten young athletes’ futures. This retrospective case series documented pediatric cases. The clinical series gives orthopedic surgeons the patterns they need to treat these rare but consequential injuries in growing bones.
plos-pone-0354258: Virtual reality in PE class — can it genuinely improve kids’ balance and coordination? This study investigated VR’s effect on middle school students’ motor skills during physical education. The findings test whether headsets belong in the gymnasium or remain a gimmick.
plos-pone-0355858: Bangladeshi license plates need automated reading — in challenging real-world conditions. This paper built a cascaded YOLO-based approach for plate identification and number recognition. The robust system brings automated traffic enforcement and tolling within reach for Bangladesh’s roads.
plos-pone-0355158: Drones need controllers that handle uncertainty gracefully. This paper proposed a novel UAV control approach: fuzzy PID-based ANFIS — FPIDANFIS. The neuro-fuzzy controller adapts to the aerodynamic unknowns that defeat rigid controllers — promising steadier flight in gusty reality.
europmc-pmc2807458: The diabetes drug metformin does more than lower blood sugar in this 2010 worm study. Researchers show it puts C. elegans into a state resembling dietary restriction and extends healthy lifespan through the AMPK, LKB1, and SKN-1 pathways. The work maps the molecular chain from drug to longer healthspan. It fueled interest in metformin as a possible anti-aging intervention.
europmc-pmc2821358: Most bladder cancers stay shallow, but some turn invasive, and telling them apart early saves lives. This 2010 paper tests whether a gene classifier can predict progression in primary non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. The authors validate the signature's predictive value. A working test could steer high-risk patients toward aggressive treatment sooner.
europmc-pmc2825658: Toxic byproducts of cells play a two-faced role in ills. This 2010 review looks at how these reactive bits push type 2 diabetes and clogged arteries ahead. The authors trace harm from bits to blood tubes. The take backs care with antioxidants while saying why quick fixes fell flat.
europmc-pmc2833258: Two tiny RNAs act as brakes on bladder cancer in this 2010 study. The authors show miR-145 and miR-133a function as tumor suppressors by directly dialing down FSCN1, a protein that helps cancer cells move. Restoring the microRNAs slowed the cancer. The work identified new molecular handles for bladder cancer therapy.
europmc-pmc2872358: Zinc is a toxin in excess and a must in small doses. This 2010 review weighs zinc's impact on human health, the essential toxin. The authors survey where it helps and harms. Their balancing act guides safe use of a double-edged nutrient.
europmc-pmc2933358: A new drug-resistance gene spread across India, Pakistan, and the UK. This 2010 paper reports the rise of NDM-1, tracing it with lab, clinical, and field data. The authors' alarm rang worldwide. Their work spurred the global fight against superbugs.
europmc-pmc2958458: Malignant belly fluid met a three-armed antibody in this 2010 trial. The authors test catumaxomab for malignant ascites from epithelial cancer in a randomized phase II/III trial. Their result backed the drug. The trial advanced a novel therapy. It was among the first trifunctional antibodies tested.
europmc-pmc2996858: Pig gum disease met stem cell therapy. This 2010 paper tests donor gum-ligament stem cells against gum disease in pigs. The authors' trial shows real healing. Their work points to tooth-saving treatments. Human trials followed the pig success. Regrown ligaments may anchor loose teeth.
europmc-pmc3000358: HIV's shell is a druggable target. This 2010 paper argues the virus's protein shell can be hit with small-molecule drugs. The authors lay out the case. Their work opened a new drug front. Capsid blockers later reached the clinic. Lenacapavir traces its roots to this pitch.
europmc-pmc3017758: Family trees need clean DNA lineups. This 2010 paper brings BMGE, software that picks the most telling parts of DNA lineups. The authors' tool trims noisy columns. Their software spread through labs. Tree builders run it before every analysis. Cleaner inputs yield truer family trees.
europmc-pmc3061958: Focus groups rarely report their size well. This 2011 paper audits how focus-group studies report their headcounts. The authors find sloppy habits. europmc-pmc6513858: Many medicines, flavors, and fragrances come from rare plants that are hard to farm or harvest sustainably. This review surveys the engineering tricks - borrowing plant genes, tuning metabolic pathways - that turn humble microbes into factories for valuable natural products.
europmc-pmc6555258: CD38 is a multitasking enzyme sitting on cell surfaces, best known for chewing through NAD+ - a molecule central to energy and aging. This review covers its many hats: tuning immune responses, fueling cancer growth, driving age-related decline, and worsening metabolic disease. Because blocking CD38 helps in animal models, it is emerging as a drug target across all four fronts.
europmc-pmc6602458: Comparing whole genomes across species reveals which genes are truly shared - the orthologs. europmc-pmc6708158: DNA methylation ticks like a clock - and its reading can reveal your biological age. A better clock means a better gauge of how fast a body is truly aging.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1058: The Pentagon's research wish lists did not add up in 2007 — GAO's report says its R&D budget asks to Congress were patchy and hard to compare. gao-gaoreports-b-299858: Computer Cite took its August 2007 contract beef to GAO, and this ruling settles it. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-758: Homeland Security's hiring halls were half-empty in 2007 — GAO's report tracks the department's push to recruit, keep, and legally mind its staff gaps. openalex-w7163351058: Certain crystals can turn light directly into electricity, no junction needed. openalex-w7203590458: Light can grab and hold objects far smaller than a cell. The authors survey the physics and the applications. An optics review of tweezers made of light.
pmc-13464958: This 2026 agriculture paper reviews strigolactones, plant hormones that can both help and hurt crops — promoting helpful fungi but also triggering parasitic weeds. pmc-13435258: This 2026 review surveys deep learning as an emerging tool for model-informed drug development — using AI to predict how drugs behave in the body during development. arxiv-2606-15958: Quantum measurement — the act of observing a quantum system — can be described as a continuous random process unfolding over time. arxiv-2606-16058: When medical studies track yes-or-no outcomes (did the patient recover?) in related groups, standard statistics can be biased. arxiv-2606-16358: LLM API routers sit between users and models, and a compromised router sees everything. arxiv-2606-16458: Coding agents write software, but this paper argues yours is secretly a roboticist: the same skills that write code — planning sequences, handling APIs, debugging — transfer to programming robots. arxiv-2606-16658: Labeling microscope slides for AI training takes expert pathologists' precious time. arxiv-2606-16758: A pure math paper about operator algebras — math frames built from operators. It studies 'deep projections' and shows the Cass criterion, a test for good behavior, can be checked locally. It is for experts in functional analysis. Near checks beat far hunts.
